client_requirement: Normal vanilla 26.1.2 client launched through the repo-native Gradle runClient adapter; protocol harnesses do not satisfy this gate.

automation_runner.client_isolation: Gradle runClient launches use per-run game directories and distinct offline usernames for primary/secondary clients.

scoped_rows_manual_pending.reason: Login compression remains scoped M100 protocol debt; no real-client compression run is available in this M94 scaffold.
Online/offline auth, duplicate names, whitelist, banlist, and op persistence remain manual-pending for public-safety review.
Falling-block landing, placement/removal, and drops need a dedicated real-client/oracle route; M94 does not count prior start-only evidence as full coverage.

scenarios.title: Join, chunk visibility, movement, disconnect, and rejoin
steps: Start Solaris with the configured debug server command and record server logs from startup.
Connect one vanilla 26.1.2 client to 127.0.0.1:25565.
Wait until the spawn area is visible and record whether missing chunks, black chunks, or lighting artifacts remain after 30 seconds.
Walk, sprint, jump, and enter/leave nearby water if present; record swim feel and any rubber-banding.
Disconnect, reconnect with the same profile, and verify position, inventory hotbar, and visible chunk state are stable.
expected_observations: Client reaches play without disconnect.
Spawn chunks become visible without persistent lighting holes.
Movement remains interactive and rejoin does not strand the player in unloaded terrain.

scenarios.title: Block edits, fluids, farming, and visible drops
steps: Break and place common solid blocks near spawn; record rejection, ghost block, or relight desyncs.
Use a door or trapdoor and a bucket where available; record visible state and nearby fluid behavior.
Exercise the named M40/M41 route: visible drops/pickup, sugar cane support/cascade/drop behavior, and nearby water movement feel.
Harvest or bonemeal one available crop or plant family and record mature/immature drops as observed by the client.
expected_observations: Block acknowledgements do not leave persistent ghost blocks.
Drops are visible, can be picked up, and disappear for the player after pickup.
Sugar cane or substitute vertical-plant behavior is classified as pass, degraded, or blocked with notes.

scenarios.title: Focused solid block placement, break, drop, and pickup
steps: Find a loaded dirt-like solid block face with adjacent loaded air within survival reach.
Use the real client destroy path to break that dirt-like block and record visible air state, item-entity visibility if observed, and held-stack pickup convergence.
Use the real client item-use path to place the picked-up dirt into a loaded adjacent air target and record visible target state plus held-stack decrement.
Keep door/trapdoor, crop/bonemeal, sugar cane, and broad fluid paths explicitly degraded rather than counting this focused run as full m94-02 coverage.
expected_observations: Breaking the dirt-like block returns it to air and restores the selected dirt stack after pickup.
Accepted placement makes the target visible as dirt and decrements the selected dirt stack.
If the visible item-entity window is too short to observe before pickup, the run records that substep as degraded.

scenarios.title: Rejected block, out-of-reach, and water-bucket fallback resync
steps: Prepare two adjacent solid blocks and first hold a matching placeable block item.
Attempt to place into the already-occupied adjacent target face and record the visible correction.
Attempt the same clicked/target face interaction from outside survival reach and record the visible correction.
Repeat the occupied-target face interaction while holding a water bucket in the selected hotbar slot.
Record whether the client immediately snaps both the clicked and target cells back to their authoritative solid states.
Record whether the held water-bucket stack remains visible and unchanged after the rejected occupied-target fallback.
Record any persistent ghost block, fluid ghost, delayed correction, disconnect, or inventory count mismatch.
expected_observations: The rejected solid placement does not leave a persistent client-visible ghost block.
The rejected out-of-reach interaction does not leave a persistent client-visible ghost block.
The rejected occupied-target water-bucket fallback does not leave a persistent client-visible ghost block or fluid ghost.
The held block and bucket stacks remain unchanged after their rejection paths.
Any visual correction delay or missing resync is recorded as blocked for B1/B3/Q2.

scenarios.title: Focused accepted water-bucket placement and pickup
steps: Find a loaded solid block face with adjacent loaded air within survival reach.
Use the real client item-use path with a held water bucket to place water into that adjacent air target.
Record that the target is visible as water and the selected held item becomes an empty bucket.
Use the real client item-use path with the empty bucket on the visible water source.
Record that the source cell is no longer fluid and the selected held item becomes a water bucket again.
Keep lava, broad fluid spread, water-lava interaction, and swim feel explicitly degraded rather than counting this focused run as full B3 coverage.
expected_observations: Accepted water placement makes the target visible as water and changes the held stack to an empty bucket.
Accepted water pickup clears the source fluid and changes the held stack back to a water bucket.
Fluid spread beyond the source cell is noted as not covered by this scenario.

scenarios.title: Inventory, crafting, containers, and common stations
steps: Move items between hotbar, inventory, and cursor; record item loss, duplication, or cursor recovery failures.
Craft one shaped or shapeless recipe and record recipe output plus inventory conservation.
Open, click in, and close a chest or barrel; repeat with one furnace-family UI if available.
Classify unavailable common stations as degraded, accepted divergence, or blocked instead of skipping silently.
expected_observations: Inventory and cursor state match visible client actions after close/reopen.
Container contents remain stable across close/open within the same run.
Unsupported stations are named explicitly in observations.

scenarios.title: Focused inventory recipe execution from oak log to planks
steps: Give the real vanilla client one oak log in the selected hotbar slot through the approved local debug command.
Send the vanilla client ServerboundPlaceRecipePacket for the inventory menu and the current configured vanilla sidecar oak_planks recipe display id.
Record that the client inventory consumes one oak log and creates four oak planks, allowing for pre-existing items from a reused player save.

Keep crafting-table UI, cursor recovery, recipe-book discovery UI, containers, stations, malformed clicks, and broad recipe execution explicitly degraded rather than counting this focused run as full M94-03 coverage.
expected_observations: The inventory recipe consumes one oak log and creates four oak planks relative to the starting inventory counts.
The run names the local recipe display id and records that this is tied to the current configured vanilla sidecar recipe layout.
No container, station, recipe-book UI, or malformed click parity is claimed.

scenarios.title: Focused two-client shared chest deposit and observation
steps: Launch two real vanilla clients through the approved Java-agent bridge runner.
Have the primary client place a chest through the real item-use path, open it, and move a held dirt stack into chest slot 0 through vanilla menu-click handling.
Have the secondary client open the same marked chest and observe chest slot 0 containing the dirt stack.
Capture screenshots from both clients and keep broad cursor recovery, malformed clicks, barrels, furnace-family UIs, and common stations explicitly degraded.
expected_observations: The primary client records accepted chest placement, container screen open, slot transfer, slot convergence, and clean screen close.
The secondary client records the same chest block, container screen open, and slot 0 containing the dirt stack.
The run does not claim broad container, station, malformed-click, or contention parity.

scenarios.title: Focused two-client shared chest live slot update
steps: Launch two real vanilla clients through the approved Java-agent bridge runner.
Have the primary client place a chest, open it, move a held dirt stack into chest slot 0 through vanilla menu-click handling, and keep that container screen open.
Have the secondary client open the same marked chest, observe dirt in slot 0, quick-move that slot into its inventory, and close the screen.
Have the primary client observe the same still-open chest screen update so slot 0 becomes empty, then close the screen.
Capture screenshots from both clients and keep broad cursor recovery, malformed clicks, barrels, furnace-family UIs, common stations, and deliberate stale-click injection explicitly degraded.
expected_observations: The primary client records accepted chest placement, container screen open, slot transfer, slot convergence, and that the screen stayed open for the peer mutation.
The secondary client records the same chest block, container screen open, slot 0 containing dirt, quick-move withdrawal, empty slot convergence, and clean screen close.
The primary client records the peer mutation arriving on the still-open container screen before it closes.
The run does not claim broad container, station, malformed-click, furnace, barrel, cursor-recovery, or deliberate stale-click parity.

scenarios.title: Signs, beds, campfires, and block-entity visuals
steps: Place or interact with a regular sign; enter plain text and verify the text is visible after closing the editor.
Use a bed to set respawn if available and record any time/sleep/weather behavior without claiming untested parity.
Place or use a campfire with a cookable item if available; record visual item state, cooked drop, and pickup behavior.
Restart the server only if the run owner has time; otherwise record persistence as not run for this scenario.
expected_observations: Plain sign text remains visible to the client after edit.
Bed and campfire behavior is classified with explicit unsupported or degraded notes.
Any restart persistence claim names the before/after artifacts.

scenarios.title: Focused regular sign placement and plain text update
steps: Find a loaded dry solid block face with adjacent loaded air within survival reach.
Use the real client item-use path with a held oak sign to place a regular floor or wall sign into that adjacent air target.
Record that the target is visible as a regular sign and the selected held item is decremented.
Wait for the real sign editor to open for the placed sign.
Send a plain four-line sign update from the real client and verify the client-side sign block entity contains those exact lines.

Keep hanging signs, waxed signs, styled/filtered/clickable text, beds, campfires, restart persistence, and after-close visual assertions explicitly degraded rather than counting this focused run as full M94-04 coverage.
expected_observations: Accepted sign placement makes the target visible as a regular sign and consumes the held oak sign.
The real sign editor opens for the placed sign.
The client-side sign block entity converges to the plain four-line text sent by the real client.
The run does not claim broad sign, bed, campfire, or persistence parity.

scenarios.title: Entities, combat, death, and respawn
steps: Observe nearby passive, hostile, or aquatic entity movement if present; record pathing stalls or visibility desyncs.
Exercise melee combat with a common mob if available and record damage, knockback, drops, and XP visibility.
Exercise one projectile or shield path only if equipment is available; otherwise mark that sub-row degraded/not run.
Die and respawn only if safe to reproduce in the prepared world; record death screen, respawn location, item/XP consequences, and reconnect state.
expected_observations: Entity presence and movement are recorded as real-client observations, not inferred from server logs.
Combat and respawn claims are limited to the exact paths executed.
Vehicles remain explicit unknown/deferred if no real-client vehicle path is available.

scenarios.title: Save/restart and two-client visibility
steps: Connect two vanilla clients and verify each can see the other join, move, and perform one block edit.
Have both clients observe one shared drop, pickup, or container interaction; record whether both views converge.
Stop Solaris cleanly, restart with the same config, reconnect, and record persisted player, chunk, container, entity, and drop state for only the paths exercised.
Record any disconnect/reconnect or contention failures as M97 candidate blockers.
expected_observations: Two-client observations are made from both clients, not only server logs.

A secondary real client observes at least one primary-client block edit, one primary-client item drop, and one primary-client item pickup removal when the second-client runner environment is configured.
Restart evidence names exact state that persisted and exact state not tested.
Visibility or contention failures are marked blocked with artifacts.

scenarios.title: Named M40/M41 water, drops, sugar cane, mobs, TPS, and lock route
steps: Run the debug server with logging sufficient to capture TPS/tick budget and lock-pressure warnings.
Use the original owner-facing water route when available: enter water, sprint-swim, surface, leave water, and record swim feel.
Break or harvest a block that produces a visible drop, pick it up, and record client/server convergence.
Exercise sugar cane support/cascade/drop behavior if the world provides it, or record the exact setup gap.
Observe nearby mob or aquatic movement and capture the server log section for TPS/lock evidence.
expected_observations: The historical water/frozen-world symptom is either reproduced, cleared by real-client observation, or left blocked.
TPS/lock log capture is attached to the run artifacts.
The scenario does not substitute protocol-harness metrics for real-client observations.

scenarios.title: Targeted enchanting table UI, XP debit, and item component
steps: Start Solaris and connect the repo-native Gradle 26.1.2 client on a fresh local world.
Use local debug setup to place an enchanting table and prepare one stone pickaxe, one lapis lazuli, and seven total XP points.
Open the vanilla enchanting screen, quick-move both inputs, and click offer button zero through the real container protocol.
Require a server-confirmed container state advance, Efficiency I on the pickaxe, total XP preserved at seven, level reduced from one to zero, and the enchanted tool returned to inventory.
expected_observations: The real client opens the vanilla EnchantmentScreen and receives a usable first offer.
The button click is accepted only after an applied server packet changes the active container state id.
Client-visible item components contain minecraft:efficiency level 1, one lapis is consumed, total XP remains seven, and one level is spent.
This targeted debug setup does not claim natural enchanting-table or lapis acquisition, bookshelf scaling, random offer parity, books, or anvils.
